steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Have you checked all the intersections?

steps.name: Seventh Tribunal Investigator
steps.text: Yes, Your Eminence. We didn't find any suspicious individuals.

steps.name: Seventh Tribunal Investigator
steps.text: We also interviewed potential witnesses nearby, but at this time we have no concrete leads.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Mushrooms might spring up on a wet pillar by themselves, but bombs don't, do they?

steps.name: Seventh Tribunal Investigator
steps.text: Huh... how could they?

steps.name: Seventh Tribunal Investigator
steps.text: With the exception of public officers of the Curia and the Shrine of Nurtury, anyone who is in possession of explosives is subject to surveillance by the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Seventh Tribunal Investigator
steps.text: It's been years since an unplanned gunshot last rang out in Laterano, never mind an explosion.
Lemuen bends down and retrieves a bomb fragment from the damaged pillar.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's pretty sophisticated. If a bomb like this was filled with standard explosives, the blast would have damaged far more than just one pillar.

steps.name: Seventh Tribunal Investigator
steps.text: Do you mean it was homemade? But why? A practical joke?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The Lateran Arms Control List was compiled by the Curia's extremely experienced explosives experts. Pretty much anything that could possibly cause a good-sized explosion is on there.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It would take considerable effort to assemble a bomb like this using materials not on the list. No one would do this for a whimsical practical joke.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Besides, today is no ordinary occasion. The second Summit of Nations is underway.
Lemuen recalls the streak of red. She feels a bit of unease, and even more perplexity.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Get me the files on recent movements around Via Jovita... correction, all of Pagus Stevonus.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Files that are clearly relevant to the case at hand should have been retrieved the moment we received our orders.
There you are!
(Pats chest) *pant*... *pant*...
Forgive me, Cardinal Lemuen. Here are the files you requested.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: My name is Amos, I'm an investigator with the Seventh Tribunal. I will be serving as your aide and conclavist.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You're late, Amos.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Patrizion said you'd be here approximately ten minutes after I arrived at the scene. Here we are, thirty minutes later.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I'm so sorry, I was preparing refreshments for the welcome ceremony. I didn't think it would be so urgent...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: (Shhh—)

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I assume you've heard about me, if the Seventh Tribunal appointed you as my aide.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: L-Lemuen the Silent...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I tolerate no excuses.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Want some ice cream, Federico? This one's on me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am not in the habit of enjoying dessert in the middle of a mission.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Besides, I already partook before leaving the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: So it was you who took the last cup from the lounge...

spans.text: who took the last cup from the lounge...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: How about you tell me why you rushed out of the Notarial Hall in such a hurry? Reward for me solving that case, so to speak.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You've been standing at this intersection for ten minutes, but there's nothing here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am under no obligation to share my private affairs with colleagues.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You said you were in the middle of a mission...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What's that sound...?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Oh—you were waiting for a confessional!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You've certainly accumulated your fair share of 'sins' as the executor with the highest rate of complaints at the Notarial Hall, but it's still a huge surprise to see you proactively seeking confession.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I expensed the cost of a City of Gold Blind Box on that field mission to Sargon, which resulted in my reimbursements being twice as much as what was actually spent on mission costs...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I went out my door with shame weighing on my heart... and spotted a confessional driving by... Anyway, long story short, I got myself an annual pass. You can borrow it.

steps.name: Mechanical Announcement
steps.text: Arrival announcement.

steps.name: Mechanical Announcement
steps.text: Automated Confessional ELCARO-001 is arriving at this station. Please line up to enjoy confessional services.

steps.name: Mechanical Announcement
steps.text: 'May all who are lost find salvation.'
The confessional enters their view, and Federico reaches out.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hahahahahaha!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Even a robot knows you don't have any emotional needs, Federico.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Virtually every Lateran comes into contact with confessionals in the course of their everyday lives. In a way, these machines hold more diverse and comprehensive data than that stored in the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: They form natural archives, revealing abnormalities.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I have arrived at certain conclusions.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hm... one second, Federico. You don't have to share your conclusions, but could you at least explain what you're looking for?
Self-reflection is part of the daily studies of the faithful. As an extension of the Church, there are almost as many confessionals in the Holy City as there are dessert carts.
These mobile public facilities roam the streets and alleys of Laterano, ensuring that citizens' emotional relief is always immediately available.
In the tiny, private space, among the holy sculptures, guns, and pleasant music, a penitent may spill their guts to the electronic confessor.
Sins could range from the shame of consuming too much sugar, to the crime of betraying one's kin or bringing harm to one's people.
After rejecting Federico, the automated confessional ELCARO-001 stops in an alley, opening its door to allow a mysterious guest to enter.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You were the one who told me to be careful.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I made sure I didn't have a tail on my butt, and you didn't give that stone-faced guy a chance to fiddle with anything.

a.text: 'He may have observed something abnormal about me.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Let's pray he doesn't catch you and tear you apart, piece-by-piece.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Of course I did. A Penguin Logistics uniform is way too conspicuous for Laterano.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I designed this outfit myself. I've only worn it once, at my graduation!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: And it's YOU we should be talking about. Do you know how weird it is to hear your voice come out of a confessional's speakers?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I hate to admit it... but yes.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It took so much effort to find the replacement materials—the market, the bakery, the playground, the school's secret shop... I went through every single source I could think of.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: And it didn't even blast the pillar in two! Any material that's even halfway decent is restricted, and no one could give an answer when I asked why.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It's not because of this 'Summit of Nations', right?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If anyone in Laterano thought the beautiful sight and sound of an explosion would be any threat to the Summit of Nations, then it's not me with the problem, it's Laterano!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: As for the Summit of Nations... they just announced the final event of the whole deal—some 'Nativity' ceremony in that shrine.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Are you telling me they built a building big enough to be seen from any corner of Laterano, not as a dessert museum, but to put on some kind of LIVE BIRTHING SHOW?!

a.text: 'You have corroborated the anomaly of your home with your own eyes, as you had hoped.'
'As you can see, this is not the Laterano you know.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It's not like I could just trust you blindly. You're just an 'electronic confessor', after all.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But now, I believe you.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: There's something REALLY wrong with Laterano. And the worst part is, nobody thinks anything's wrong at all!

a.text: 'The shrine, and the ceremony. If all the anomalies are centered around the two of them...'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Then it's on us to bomb them, isn't it?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If I figured out how to blow up a shrine that big using only common household items, shouldn't every university in Laterano give me a lifetime achievement award?

a.text: 'As long as you reawaken their love of explosions.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Can you believe it? The Laterans need someone to remind them that they love explosions? Sounds like a nightmare, doesn't it? Shouldn't take more than an afternoon at the Firearms Workshop to do the job.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh yeah! The Firearms Workshop! The workshops may be closed, but the people are still around!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I know what you're gonna say. It's too dangerous. Firearms Workshop is the first place they would look if anything happened, right?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Don't worry, I'll be careful. You do the same, and don't get yourself taken apart. That's my job, once this is all over and done with.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Anyway... Welcome to Laterano!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: My investigation is now concluded. Thank you all for your contributions.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We can go back to the Seventh Tribunal once we've signed off on the paperwork. If the refreshments at the welcome ceremony haven't gone stale yet, may I count on your assistance in eliminating them with extreme prejudice?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I would like you to accompany me to see the gun-knights, Amos.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Is there a problem?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: If by 'gun-knights' you mean Reverend Patrizion, I... I'll ask Joshua to accompany you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Explain.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: There was an incident a decade ago, when a nomadic abbey was escorting prisoners back to Laterano. A terrible fight broke out between a gun-knight and her cohort...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: By the time the Curia sent someone, much blood had been spilled, and the gun-knight had fallen.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: She was exiled from Laterano and has not been heard from since.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I've heard of the case.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: That gun-knight was my wife. It was Reverend Patrizion who led the clean-up task force and exiled her.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You've been with the Seventh Tribunal far longer than I have, Conclavist Amos. I don't need to remind you of our duty, and the duty of the gun-knights—

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: No, no, you misunderstand.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: My wife was entirely at fault.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Any Sankta who raises their patron firearm against one of their own must be judged by the Law and be expelled from Paradise.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I am in no position to criticize Reverend Gun-Knight Patrizion... however, I can't bring myself to see him like this either.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Is this how you've handled any previous dealings with the gun-knights?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I... yes. I'm sorry.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I-I'm very sorry. Give me five minutes, I'll try to collect myself, and maybe I can go with you...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I don't mean to reprimand you. I just think that this is part of what we do at the Seventh Tribunal.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We spend our time seeing people we don't want to see, and not seeing the people we want to see. Or worse—seeing the people we want to see in the worst ways possible.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I hated handing down instructions to Mostima and the others.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: But they said you volunteered to join the Seventh Tribunal...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Because there's a lot I can do here.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The same goes for you, Amos.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Thank you. But I don't really have aspirations. It was like that when my wife was around, and even more so after she left...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: There's a lot at the Seventh Tribunal that needs doing. For example, there are still several Firearms Workshops that need attention.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's our first priority right now. The seizure of the Firearms Workshops must proceed without a hitch in order to prevent any more explosions.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'll leave it to you. Be quick, won't you?

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Are you tired?

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: You've gone through six rows of wheat with your sickle since dawn. Perhaps you should take a break by the haystacks.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'm not so frail. Besides...

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Besides?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Nothing. I just wanted to see where the fields end.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I can't make out the boundary. Even my music can't penetrate it.
You'll have to work harder!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We meet again, Sister Hildegard.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Good afternoon, Arturia.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I brought your lunch—bread, some ice cream crackers, and a large mug of craft beer!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Thank you. Work harder, you said?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What I mean is, there's plenty for us to do.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Look at the golden stalks, the undulating waves of wheat... it's another bumper harvest in Laterano.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Setting aside our own food stocks, Landen Monastery will be able to put twice as much grain as usual into cystymilk bread and craft beer this year. It'll be a good source of income!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Why are you laughing?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The way you talk about life makes me appreciate this prison even more, Sister Hildegard.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The respect you show for this prison makes me appreciate you even more, Arturia.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I'm very curious about your transgression. I heard the other nuns saying that your music is beautiful, but dangerous.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I have a question.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If I recall correctly, Landen Monastery was founded to protect the Pope and important clerics of the Lateran Church...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Which makes me wonder when this place became a prison.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Is it not protecting... er, important clerics and the peace of Laterano, to put certain individuals of note under observation?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The significance of Landen Monastery has never changed.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Besides, the more important the monastery is to the Holy City, the less likely we will fall insolvent.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How did you acclimate to this place so quickly as a Liberi?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I grew up here.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Oh, I almost forgot. This is what you requested yesterday.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Gratias.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What made you want to read The Saints' Travels all of a sudden?

spans.text: What made you want to read

steps.text: Arturia gazes into the distance.
Behind her, the worn image of the monastery; before her, a golden sea of wheat. The wheat field runs to the edge of the Holy City, and seems to extend infinitely into the distance.
The breeze blowing through the wheat makes nary a sound. Laterano seems to slumber.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Penance, of course. What other reason might a prisoner have?
